reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer (packet-only), 2026-07-30 post-fix re-review batch

samples_reviewed.question_text: Daniel has ₱4 in bills and ₱0 in coins. How much money does Daniel have in all?
Kuya Bien has ₱0 in bills and ₱3 in coins. How much money does Kuya Bien have in all?
In a pictograph, Lara's group collected 41 ribbons and another group collected 30 ribbons. How many more did Lara's group collect?
In a pictograph, Coach Roel's group collected 25 water bottles and another group collected 20 water bottles. How many more did Coach Roel's group collect?
Ate Cara has ₱12 in bills and ₱1 in coins. How much money does Ate Cara have in all?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The competency requires addition and subtraction 'with 3 to 4 numbers of up to 2 digits', but every one of the five samples combines exactly TWO numbers: seed 42 is ₱4 + ₱0, seed 46 is ₱12 + ₱1, seed 44 is 41 - 30, seed 45 is 25 - 20. Not a single item asks the student to combine three or four quantities, so the defining requirement of this lc is never exercised. Seeds 42 and 43 are weaker still: with a ₱0 operand ('Daniel has ₱4 in bills and ₱0 in coins', answer 4) the item degenerates to reading one number off the page and no addition is actually performed.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The wording names three sub-cases that must appear: 3-number problems, 4-number problems, and money problems. Only the money sub-case is generated (seeds 42, 43, 46, all in pesos). The 3-number and 4-number cases are entirely absent across all five seeds - the maximum operand count observed is 2. There is also no mixed add-and-subtract item: each sample is purely additive ('How much money does Ate Cara have in all?') or purely subtractive ('How many more did Lara's group collect?'), yet mixing is the natural multi-number case this competency implies.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Demand is far below Grade 3 Quarter 2. 'Daniel has ₱4 in bills and ₱0 in coins. How much money does Daniel have in all?' (answer 4) and 'Kuya Bien has ₱0 in bills and ₱3 in coins' (answer 3) are single-digit or no-op computations a Grade 1 learner would find trivial. Even the hardest sampled item, 41 - 30 = 11, is a one-step two-digit subtraction with no regrouping. Sentence structure and vocabulary are appropriately simple and readable for Grade 3, but the reasoning required - one operation on two small numbers - falls well short of combining 3 to 4 numbers.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Only two templates recur across five seeds, and both are word problems: a bills-plus-coins money frame (seeds 42, 43, 46, identical apart from names and amounts) and a pictograph comparison frame (seeds 44, 45, likewise identical apart from names and objects). There is no pure-computation or number-sentence variant, no missing-addend orientation, and no change/take-away money situation such as paying and receiving change. The contexts that do appear are coherent and use natural Filipino register (Kuya Bien, Ate Cara, Coach Roel, peso amounts), which is a genuine strength.

competency_alignment.rationale: Progression across the seeds varies only operand magnitude - ₱4 + ₱0 up to ₱12 + ₱1, and 25 - 20 up to 41 - 30 - never the operand count this competency is built on. Harder seeds are harder only because the numerals are larger, so the axis being exercised is 'size of a 2-digit number', which belongs to earlier addition/subtraction lcs rather than 'solve problems with 3 to 4 numbers'. The pictograph framing ('In a pictograph, Coach Roel's group collected 25 water bottles') also leans toward a data-representation competency while supplying no actual pictograph, adding words without adding the targeted reasoning.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The 2-digit ceiling is respected - the largest operand is 41 and the largest answer 13 - so nothing exceeds the stated range, but the floor is badly underused. Three of five items use single-digit or zero operands (₱4, ₱0, ₱3, ₱1), and ₱0 is not a legitimate value for 'up to 2 digits' money work because it removes the computation entirely. Since no item combines 3 to 4 two-digit numbers, totals never reach the larger sums such problems would produce, leaving the effective numeric range well below the competency's intent.
